target_customer: Frontier labs and humanoid or robotics companies that need real-world human demonstration data
problem: Physical AI is bottlenecked on real-world data such as egocentric video, 3D scans and multimodal capture from industrial and residential settings.
business_model: Data vendor: pays or partners with businesses to capture worker data and sells it to robotics developers (no buyers named publicly)

founders.name: Rohan Seelamsetty
education: University of Pennsylvania, Computation and Cognition
founders.background_notes: YC page cites debate and factory floor and political campaign experience.

founders.name: Dev Karpe
prior_employers: Supply chain operations in the office of a Fortune 500 CEO

founders.name: Tommy Li
education: UPenn, BSE computer science and finance
founders.background_notes: Published IEEE researcher per the YC page.

competitors.name: Scale AI
competitors.what: Runs a recorder network for egocentric robotics data and helped set up the EgoVerse dataset consortium
competitors.traction_then: Reported to hold about 100,000 hours of robotics footage (a blog report, unverified)

competitors.name: Micro1
competitors.what: Distributed workforce capturing human video for humanoid training
competitors.traction_then: About 4,000 contributors in 71 countries, reportedly 160,000 hours a month (unverified)

competitors.name: Objectways
competitors.what: Egocentric and RGB-D data for robotics
competitors.traction_then: President says about 1,000 hours a day (unverified)

technical_complexity.rationale: Multimodal capture rigs, data quality and annotation pipelines across many sites are operationally hard, but not research-grade.

defensibility.rationale: Access agreements with large conglomerates and diverse real environments are hard to copy, though larger labelers pursue the same data.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large data vendors and robotics firms were already collecting egocentric data. No acquisition of Praxis Robotics found.

market_need_then: Egocentric human video is widely viewed as key to humanoid training; reports cite demand of 200,000 to 300,000 hours and NVIDIA research on 20,000 hours of pretraining (vendor blogs, unverified).

branding.domain_note: Uses praxisrobotics.io; the site headline is 'Great machines will be forged by human intuition'.
branding.brand_signature: Great machines will be forged by human intuition

brand_strength.rationale: A recurring generic name shared with several other Praxis companies, with only one startup profile of press.

outcome_analysis: Praxis Robotics is a three-person Summer 2026 company with finance, venture and robotics research backgrounds, claiming access to 60,000 workers and 150+ environment types. A Runtimewire profile notes it names no buyer or paying customer, and no funding beyond YC was found. It is early, with big vendors in the same market, so the outcome is open.
notes: Company website fetch returned only a headline, so product details come from the YC page and a Runtimewire profile. Competitor source dates are not shown on the pages found, so source_date is null and the as_of is approximate. CB Insights and Dealroom funding entries for 'Praxis' refer to other companies and are excluded. Traction numbers (60k workers, 150+ environments) are company claims.
